title: Coherence of finite-coefficient pro-etale pullback stalk comparisons
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$ be morphisms of schemes, with small pro-etale sites and compatible small skeletons and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the constant coefficient sheaves, their canonical inverse-image identifications preserving constant sections [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and the derived pullbacks of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For a bounded complex $H$ of $A_X$-module sheaves and a geometric point $v:s=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z$ [def-weil-geometric-point], write $H_u$ for the termwise geometric stalk complex at a geometric point $u$, with stalks as in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For a morphism $t:T\to S$, geometric point $u:s\to T$, and coefficient complex $M$ on $S$, there is a natural $A$-linear isomorphism
$$c_{t,u,M}:(Lt^*M)_u\xrightarrow{\sim}M_{tu}.$$
It is the canonical inverse-image stalk comparison, normalized as follows using [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: for a sheaf $M$, a representative consists of $a\in M(V)$, a site morphism $\theta:U\to T\times_SV$, and a pointed lift $u':s\to U$ over $u$. Its image is $[V,\operatorname{pr}_V\theta u',a]$. The inverse sends $[V,w,a]$ to the pullback-unit section on $T\times_SV$ with pointed lift $(u,w)$.

Let $\chi_{h,f}:L(fh)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*Lf^*$ be the canonical composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Then
$$c_{fh,v,H}=c_{f,hv,H}\circ c_{h,v,Lf^*H}\circ(\chi_{h,f,H})_v.$$
Under the canonical identity-pullback identification, $c_{\mathrm{id},u,H}=\mathrm{id}_{H_u}$. For $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$, let $r_{u,\alpha,M}:M_u\to M_{u\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha)}$ send $[V,w,a]$ to $[V,w\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),a]$. Then
$$r_{tu,\alpha,M}\circ c_{t,u,M}=c_{t,u\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha),M}\circ r_{u,\alpha,Lt^*M}.$$
These equalities are natural in the coefficient complex and hold in the ordinary derived categories after localization at quasi-isomorphisms.
